label: GO step when the agent chooses a1 (fires on ~1/3 of them)
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2) and almost only when the agent picks a1: 98% of activation mass is on GO steps where the policy argmax is a1. Recorded model_act == 1 (the agent computes its own choice, so no future variable); action == 1 scores almost the same. But it is active on only ~32% of those steps, so precision is low. Restricting to a confident a1 logit (choice > 8) raises F1 to 0.57 but drops mass recall to 0.82. Firing also drops off late in the episode (trials 80-99 nearly silent; ep_trial < 80 gives precision 0.37). Magnitude: largest on an a1 GO that comes right after an unrewarded a2 trial, i.e. a switch to a1 (top examples reach 1.0), then it shrinks over consecutive a1 trials (about 0.24, 0.12, ...) and goes up again after an unrewarded trial. Overall, switch trials are only slightly overrepresented (precision 0.39 vs 0.31 for stays). Previous reward, transition type and the good state do not explain which a1 GO steps fire. Never fires on a2 choices, at D1/D2, or on steps with a reward or state input.
